misconceptions.description: Treating any data recording as 'just monitoring' regardless of aggregation depth, learner visibility, or opt-out reality
misconceptions.trigger: learner labels webcam emotion detection as 'engagement monitoring'
misconceptions.feedback: Aggregation depth, asymmetry of access, and inability to opt out distinguish surveillance from monitoring. Bounded, learner-visible, opt-out-real records are monitoring; combined-stream, learner-blind, mandatory records are surveillance.

misconceptions.description: Treating engagement metrics as evidence of autonomous motivation
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites session-length increase as proof of motivated learning
misconceptions.feedback: SDT distinguishes autonomous motivation from controlled motivation. Manufactured engagement produces controlled motivation that collapses without the manipulative cue.

misconceptions.description: Treating gamification mechanics as automatically pedagogical
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds streaks and badges and labels the change 'gamification for learning'
misconceptions.feedback: Variable-ratio reinforcement borrows from slot-machine design. Some gamification supports learning; some exploits limited self-regulation. The distinction requires explicit pedagogical justification, not default deployment.

misconceptions.description: Equating respect for learner autonomy with design abstinence ('do nothing')
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues autonomy means refusing to scaffold or recommend at all
misconceptions.feedback: Autonomy means volitional control. Design supports autonomy by surfacing what the system does, giving granular control, and making exit real. Active design is consistent with autonomy; manipulative or hidden design is not.
